title: DEPS, gclient and what replaced goma
dek: Chromium is one git repository plus a 5,188-line file that declares 451 more dependencies across three transports. This is how gclient sync reads that file, how rollers rewrite it about 940 times a week, how the compiler is pinned in text — and how the distributed build underneath went from goma to reclient to Siso.
description: Chromium declares 451 dependencies in one 5,188-line DEPS file. How gclient sync reads it, how rollers rewrite it, and how goma became Siso.
og_description: A teardown of Chromium's dependency machine: depot_tools, the DEPS grammar, gclient sync step by step, submodules, autorollers, toolchain pinning — and goma, reclient and Siso.
twitter_description: 451 dependencies in one file. How gclient sync reads it, how rollers rewrite it 940 times a week, and how goma became Siso.

sections.title: One repository, 451 dependencies
sections.brief: THESIS: Chromium is not a monorepo. It is one git repository plus a declarative description of everything else it needs, and the program that reads that description never executes it. Open on the census at the subject commit (chromium/src@f288fed6, chrome/VERSION 156.0.8067.0, checked out 2026-09-18): src/DEPS is 5,188 lines of Python syntax declaring 451 dependency entries — 273 git, 147 CIPD, 31 GCS — carrying 153 CIPD packages and 87 GCS objects, alongside 143 vars, 61 hooks, 9 recursedeps, 24 allowed_hosts and 49 root include_rules [src/DEPS, counted by parsing it with depot_tools' own gclient_eval.Exec and independently with ast.parse; dossier §1.1 and verification V11]. Quote the docs verbatim: "gclient supports three dependency types: git, gcs and cipd" [src/docs/dependencies.md:9-10] from the docs. Name gclient's three on-disk artefacts from its own module docstring — .gclient (the solutions), .gclient_entries (a cache of what is checked out) and each module's DEPS [depot_tools/gclient.py:6-20]. Then set up the handoff that organises the whole post: a sync ends by writing src/build/config/gclient_args.gni holding exactly the 17 variables src/DEPS exports [src/DEPS:39-58; depot_tools/gclient.py:1612-1631], and build/toolchain/siso.gni imports that file [src/build/toolchain/siso.gni:3-14]. Everything before that line is dependency description; everything after it is the distributed build — goma, then reclient, then Siso. State the thesis the rest of the piece proves, in one paragraph: the declarative file is cheap to change and the ecosystem that parses it is not, so Chromium keeps every old interface alive while the new mechanism carries the load underneath (dossier §1.15). Plant two "you are here" facts to be paid off later without explaining them yet: git_dependencies = 'SYNC' three years after a stage 2 scheduled for 2023 Q4 [src/DEPS:35-37], and reclient still pinned a year after its announced removal [src/build/toolchain/rbe.gni:29-31]. OWNED ELSEWHERE, do not pre-empt: the grammar (§03), the sync algorithm (§04), byte totals in detail (§05), the toolchain (§06), rollers (§07–§08), submodules (§09), goma (§10), Siso (§11). Name them only. Do not restate the badge callout — the stitcher emits it above this section. Relative links go up two levels (../../).

sections.title: The tool belt and the three files
sections.brief:
THESIS: depot_tools is a tool belt, fetch is a recipe runner, and the interesting division of labour is the one between the three files — .gclient is the user's, DEPS is the project's, .gclient_entries is gclient's own memory. Facts to use. depot_tools' README names fetch, gclient, git cl and roll-dep as the important tools and calls gn, autoninja, siso and ninja thin wrappers that locate binaries inside the checkout [depot_tools/README.md:10-33]; it needs Python 3.8+ and self-updates on every gclient invocation unless DEPOT_TOOLS_UPDATE=0 [depot_tools/README.md:3-5,73-76; depot_tools/gclient:8-28]. The wrappers bundle nothing: gn.py asks gclient_paths for the primary solution and runs /buildtools//gn, itself a CIPD dep [depot_tools/gn.py:5-12,40-52]. depot_tools is recursively a Chromium dependency: src/third_party/depot_tools is pinned at 0306e468 — the exact revision of the clone this post reads — and a hook disables self-update for that copy [src/DEPS:2211-2212; src/DEPS:4456-4466]. Note the three interpreters so the reader is not confused later: host python3 3.8+ for depot_tools, the uv-backed vpython3 environment [src/vpython.toml:14], and the hermetic CIPD cpython3 3.11.9 that GN uses as script_executable [src/DEPS:295; src/.gn:12] (dossier D6). fetch chromium: fetch_configs/chromium.py returns a spec whose single solution is {name: 'src', url: https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src.git, custom_deps: {}, custom_vars: {}}, and GclientGitCheckout.init runs `gclient config --spec …` then `gclient sync`, adding --nohooks / --no-history / --with_branch_heads as asked, then sets diff.ignoreSubmodules=dirty [depot_tools/fetch.py:142-166]. fetch android/ios/chrome are aliases re-invoking the same config with extra props. fetch --git-cache (June 2026) sets cache_dir and cache_mode='bootstrap' [depot_tools/fetch.py:225-231,323-332]. The documented entry point is still `fetch --nohooks chromium`, with the cache "~30 GB for Chromium" and "30 minutes on even a fast connection" [src/docs/linux/build_instructions.md:70-108] from the docs. .gclient is Python-shaped data, not a program — gclient_eval.ParseLocalConfig accepts only literal assignments [depot_tools/gclient_eval.py:699-774]. A solution carries name, url, deps_file, managed, custom_deps, custom_vars, custom_hooks, protocol_override; top-level keys add target_os/target_cpu (unioned with the host through DEPS_OS_CHOICES, linux→'unix'), cache_dir, cache_mode and root hooks [depot_tools/gclient.py:2160-2256; :2043-2059]. Correct the folklore about `managed` with dates: fetch chromium has written managed: False explicitly since 2013-08-22; the June 2016 attempt to flip gclient's own default was reverted three weeks later for breaking iOS release branches; the durable flip is 2026-06-16 [depot_tools/gclient.py:2225,4366-4375; dossier §1.4 and D2]. gclient_paths.FindGclientRoot climbs from cwd to .gclient and validates through .gclient_entries — that is how gn and ninja find the tree from any subdirectory. CODE EXCERPT (1): depot_tools/fetch_configs/chromium.py:15-38, the whole fetch_spec. Escape < > & inside 
.
OWNED ELSEWHERE: the DEPS grammar itself (§03); what sync does with the solution (§04); cache_mode mechanics (§04/§05).

sections.title: A grammar that is parsed, never run
sections.brief:
THESIS: DEPS looks like Python and is never executed. gclient_eval parses it to an AST, walks a whitelist, and the whole expressive power of the file is four things — variables, string interpolation, conditions, and three dependency shapes.
Facts and paths. gclient_eval.Exec runs ast.parse, accepts only single-target assignments to plain names with no re-definition, and allows constants, lists, tuples, dicts without duplicate keys, Str(...), Var(...) and the + and % binary operators [depot_tools/gclient_eval.py:483-534; :360-480]. Every string constant then goes through a str.format-style expansion of {name} placeholders via a _SafeFormatter that rejects attribute and item access — which is exactly why a CIPD package template must be spelled ${{platform}} [depot_tools/gclient_eval.py:51-71; src/DEPS:1172]. Var() reads a variable; Str() wraps one so it is emitted verbatim into GN args instead of being evaluated as a condition [depot_tools/gclient_eval.py:74-93; depot_tools/gclient.py:1626-1631]. Precedence, stated once and never again: DEPS vars < parent vars < built-ins (checkout_android … checkout_win, host_os, checkout_x64 …, host_cpu) < .gclient custom_vars, which may only override names that already exist [depot_tools/gclient.py:1898-1922; :1924-1940]. The parsed result is validated against a schema declaring the legal top-level keys [depot_tools/gclient_eval.py:258-357]. Conditions are their own whitelist language — and/or/not, ==, !=, in — with string-valued variables recursively evaluated as expressions [depot_tools/gclient_eval.py:777-892]; deps_os and hooks_os, where they survive, are folded into checkout_<os> conditions [depot_tools/gclient_eval.py:572-686], a 2018-05-16 change that is the last trace of the pre-2017 model.
Cover the four structures the ask names: vars (143 of them: 98 strings, 36 bools, 9 Str()); conditions (320 of the 451 entries are conditional); dep_type (git / cipd / gcs, with the exact value shapes — None, 'url@revision', a git dict, a CIPD dict with packages carrying version or version_file, a GCS dict with bucket plus objects carrying object_name, sha256sum, size_bytes, generation) [depot_tools/gclient_eval.py:181-236]; hooks (a flat list, with the note that `pattern` is a documented no-op under git — see §04); recursedeps (9 entries: angle, dawn, instrumented_libs, openscreen, devtools-frontend, clank, the internal optimization-guide, ios_internal, webpagereplay [src/DEPS:5170-5188]) with the fact that `recursion = N` is ignored with a warning since 2018-06-11; and gclient_gn_args_file / gclient_gn_args, the 17 exported variables [src/DEPS:39-58]. Mention that three git-dep spellings coexist in one file [src/DEPS:322-332; :3342-3343; :3075-3076].
CODE EXCERPTS (2): src/DEPS:35-58 verbatim (git_dependencies, gclient_gn_args_file, the gclient_gn_args list) and depot_tools/gclient_eval.py:447-468 (the Var() arm of _convert, including the KeyError text "was used as a variable, but was not declared in the vars dict" and the Add/Mod arms). Escape < > & inside <code>/<pre>.
OWNED ELSEWHERE: what the parsed tree is then used for (§04); hook contents and ordering (§04, §06); the SYNC state (§09).

sections.title: What gclient sync actually does
sections.brief:
THESIS: gclient sync is a scheduler with a fixed epilogue. The order is the mechanism: everything parallel happens first, and five things happen strictly after the queue drains.
Walk it in order. CMDsync parses options (--jobs defaults to max(8, CPUs)); LoadCurrentConfig walks up to .gclient and validates through .gclient_entries that the cwd belongs to this checkout; RunOnDeps('update') builds an ExecutionQueue [depot_tools/gclient.py:4769-4772; :5409-5414; :2786-2845]. The queue is dependency-aware, not merely parallel: a Dependency starts only when its requirements — its parent, all top-level solutions for second-level nodes, and any dep whose path is a prefix of its own — have finished, and never concurrently with another job on the same repository URL [depot_tools/gclient_utils.py:1047-1059; depot_tools/gclient.py:672-708]. It prints "Still working on:" after 60 s (a 2014-04-08 behaviour) and, since 2026-04-16, "STALL DETECTED: gclient has been silent for 5 minutes." after 300 s [depot_tools/gclient_utils.py:977,1085; dossier V07/D5] — get that split right, the two timers are twelve years apart.
Per dependency: check out, then, only if allowed to recurse, parse DEPS, run pre_deps_hooks, enqueue children. Recursion is capped at two levels ("Only solution level and immediate DEPS are processed", hard-coded 2010-06-28); children inherit the parent's condition, ANDed in [depot_tools/gclient.py:2084-2086; :798-806]. Git mechanics: a fresh dep is cloned with `git clone --no-checkout --progress [--shared] <url> <tmpdir>` and the .git moved into place; --no-history does git init plus a depth-1 fetch; HEAD is left detached [depot_tools/gclient_scm.py:1742-1821]. An existing dep first tries the submodule fast path — if the gitlink already equals the pinned hash nothing runs — then handles URL switches, fetches only when the SHA is not already local, and branches into five documented cases (detached HEAD, non-tracking branch, DEPS moved to a hash, fast-forward merge, branch switch needing --force) [depot_tools/gclient_scm.py:1109-1121; :1241-1266; :1198-1214]. Underneath sits git_cache.Mirror: one bare repo per URL, populated under a lock, re-bootstrapped from gs://chromium-git-cache/v2/<name>/<n>.ready when absent, empty or holding more than 50 packs — and only ten googlesource hosts have snapshots [depot_tools/git_cache.py:182-201; :781-819; :137-171].
The epilogue, in this order and only after the queue drains: write gclient_args.gni if it changed; _RemoveUnversionedGitDirs against the previous .gclient_entries (delete only with -D, restoring submodule mount points with `git restore`); one `cipd ensure` for every package from every DEPS via a generated ensure file ($ParanoidMode CheckPresence, $OverrideInstallMode copy, @Subdir blocks); then hooks [depot_tools/gclient.py:2895-2943; :2554-2766]. GCS objects are the exception — they download during the tree walk, verified against both sha256sum and size_bytes, auto-extracted, tracked by three hidden marker files [depot_tools/gclient.py:3318-3410]. Hooks are flat, root-first then depth-first; `pattern` is a documented no-op under git so all of them run; a failure exits 2 [depot_tools/gclient.py:1698-1729]. Close on the shape of real work: 154 of 273 git deps, 24 of 147 CIPD, 17 of 31 GCS and 13 of 61 hooks on a default Linux x64 host.
CODE EXCERPTS (2): depot_tools/gclient.py:2825-2845 (the post-queue ordering) and depot_tools/gclient_scm.py:1109-1121 (the gitlink fast path, with "Using submodule information to skip check").
OWNED ELSEWHERE: the bot variant and byte totals (§05); hook contents (§06); why the gitlink exists (§09).

sections.title: A checkout on a bot, and in bytes
sections.short: On a bot, and in bytes
sections.brief:
THESIS: The same algorithm runs on every builder, wrapped in one Python script, and it is measurable. Give the reader the real command line and the real byte totals.
The bot path. CI builders do not run fetch. Every chromium/src builder is launched through the infra/chromium/bootstrapper executable, which pulls the tools/build recipe bundle at refs/heads/main and reads the builder's properties.json out of chromium/src itself; the 2026 tree generates 1,066 such files, 584 ci and 438 try [src/infra/config/generated/luci/cr-buildbucket.cfg:17-37]. The recipe calls prepare_checkout, which forwards to bot_update.ensure_checkout with cwd [CACHE]/builder [depot_tools/recipes/recipe_modules/bot_update/api.py:306-396]. Inside bot_update.py the order is fixed: core.trustctime false, read or create the git-cache epoch, wipe the workspace if .dirty_bot_checkout exists, then per solution `git cache populate` (only when the pin is missing or --enforce_fetch), `git clone --no-checkout --local --shared <mirror> src`, `git fetch origin <pin>`, `git checkout --force`, `git clean -dff`, write .gclient, then `gclient sync --verbose --reset --force --upstream --nohooks --noprehooks --delete_unversioned_trees --revision src@unmanaged`, then `gclient revinfo -a --ignore-dep-type cipd --output-json`. Every subprocess has a 300 s `ps auxwwf` timer and a 1200 s stale-process killer.
Two measured builds, both 2026-09-22. CI Linux Builder (8669987184970100865), cold builder cache, six-day-old git cache: populate fetched 188,439 objects in 1.7 minutes, checkout 3.4 minutes, gclient sync 6.6 minutes (167 deps cloned --shared from the local mirror, one cipd ensure), revinfo 0.1 minutes; disk 167 GB → 192 GB of 290 GB. The try compilator (8669976255482942481) did it in 80 seconds on a warm cache with --patch_ref …refs/changes/99/8424399/3, applied as a fetch, a `git cherry-pick --keep-redundant-commits` and a `git reset --soft`. Two knobs are dormant: no chromium/src builder sets clobber, no_history or shallow (0 of 1,666 builder_spec entries), and bot_update_experiments — the only route to `--experiment no-sync` — is in none of the 1,066 properties files.
The bytes. GCS is exact because DEPS declares size_bytes: a default Linux x64 checkout activates 17 GCS entries with 46 objects totalling 917,327,049 bytes, dominated by the Meet GPU test bundle (276,997,227 B — the "~278MB" the DEPS comment warns of [src/DEPS:1220-1232]) and the Rust tarball (276,524,576 B); clang is only 63,156,692 B. CIPD sizes are absent from DEPS and were resolved live: 26 packages, 621,162,316 bytes, led by the JDK at 148,797,791 B. The git side comes from the public cache bucket: the chromium/src snapshot is 15,481,300,760 bytes in 46 files (seven packs capped at 2 GiB, 842 MB of .idx, a 58.7 MB commit-graph, 47,639 refs), and the 148 active deps with snapshots cover 142 repositories worth 8,055,808,935 unique bytes. Total ≈ 25.1 GB unique (25.70 GB by checkout path, because JetStream is mirrored at three paths and Speedometer at five); the non-git part is 1,538,489,365 B — 6.1% of bytes for 41 of 195 active entries. Both totals are lower bounds: six active deps have no snapshot (dossier C07/V02).
CODE EXCERPT (1): the bot_update execution details from logs.chromium.org build 8669987184970100865 (≤ 23 lines).
OWNED ELSEWHERE: the sync algorithm (§04); GCS contents (§06); roll traffic (§08).

sections.title: Pinning a toolchain in text
sections.brief:
THESIS: Chromium's compiler is not installed, it is pinned — and the most important structural fact for a 2026 reader is that clang is no longer fetched by a hook at all.
The clang story. tools/clang/scripts/update.py holds CLANG_REVISION = 'llvmorg-24-init-7747-g62397f8b' with CLANG_SUB_REVISION = 29 [src/tools/clang/scripts/update.py:36-47], but since June 2024 src/third_party/llvm-build/Release+Asserts is a first-class GCS dep in bucket chromium-browser-clang, conditioned on `not llvm_force_head_revision`, with 23 objects — six each for Linux_x64, Mac and Win and five for Mac_arm64, which has no runtime-library package — each with its own condition [src/DEPS:924-1091]. Get the count right: it is 23, not 24, and "6 per host platform" is wrong (dossier D4/V04). GN then cross-checks: config("clang_revision") reads the cr_build_revision stamp shipped inside the tarball, parses CLANG_REVISION and CLANG_SUB_REVISION back out of update.py, and asserts equality with the message "Did you forget to gclient sync?" [src/build/config/compiler/BUILD.gn:1480-1592]. Rust is pinned in lockstep because rustc is built against the pinned LLVM — its package name is <RUST_REVISION>-<RUST_SUB_REVISION>-<CLANG_REVISION> [src/tools/rust/update_rust.py:69-86].
The roll, briefly (the figure carries the detail): upload_revision.py resolves the newest LLVM commit, computes the revision with `git describe --long --abbrev=8 --match=*llvmorg-*-init`, patches both update scripts and fires the *_upload_clang / *_upload_rust bots [src/tools/clang/scripts/upload_revision.py:151-215]; package.py uploads to staging with x-goog-if-generation-match:0, so a reused hash silently skips the upload [src/docs/updating_clang.md:90-96]; a permissioned Googler promotes staging to production and runs sync_deps.py, which stats and hashes each object and calls `gclient setdep --revision=path@object,sha256,size,generation` [src/tools/clang/scripts/sync_deps.py:56-153]. Cadence: every two to four weeks [src/docs/clang.md:3-5].
Everything else, same pattern, different transport — this is the section's ledger figure: GN, ninja, Siso, luci-go and CPython 3.11.9 are CIPD packages [src/DEPS:1169-1197; :2773-2791; :2344-2366]; clang-format binaries and the nine Debian bullseye sysroots are content-addressed GCS objects, the sysroot object name being literally the tarball's sha256 [src/DEPS:754-808; :637-752]; libc++ and friends are git sub-repos whose revision must also be copied into buildtools/deps_revisions.gni [src/DEPS:524-528]; the NDK and Android SDK are conditional CIPD deps [src/DEPS:1847-1858]; Windows and macOS keep script-driven hooks [src/DEPS:4525-4538]; PGO profiles stay hooks on purpose because they weigh about a gigabyte and change roughly four times a day [src/DEPS:4923-5027].
Close on the version string, which is the cheapest illustration of the whole design: the unconditional lastchange hook runs build/util/lastchange.py, which does `git log -1 --format=%H %ct` filtered by ^Change-Id:, reads the Cr-Commit-Position footer and writes LASTCHANGE=<sha>-refs/heads/main@{#N} [src/build/util/lastchange.py:153-189; :772-796]; build/util/version.py combines that with chrome/VERSION (MAJOR=156 MINOR=0 BUILD=8067 PATCH=0) for every downstream @KEY@ substitution [src/build/util/version.py:33-88]. Mention the 61-hook list is now mostly housekeeping: vpython3_common first, landmines, disable_depot_tools_selfupdate, the five lastchange hooks, legacy .sha1 downloads (ciopfs, dsymutil, rc, apache_win32), Fuchsia/ChromeOS extras, configure_siso near the end.
CODE EXCERPTS (2): src/tools/clang/scripts/update.py:36-52 (the DO-NOT-CHANGE comment block plus CLANG_REVISION / CLANG_SUB_REVISION / PACKAGE_VERSION / RELEASE_VERSION) and src/build/config/compiler/BUILD.gn:1495-1519 (the assert with "Did you forget to gclient sync?").
OWNED ELSEWHERE: what gclient does with a GCS dep mechanically (§04); setdep's internals (§07); who fires the roll CLs (§08); Siso's use of gclient_args.gni (§11).

sections.title: Editing DEPS by machine
sections.brief:
THESIS: DEPS is editable by program precisely because it is parsed twice — once to an AST and once to a token stream — so a roll rewrites one string token and nothing else moves.
The mechanism. _NodeDict keeps the tokenize token stream alongside the parsed values, RenderDEPSFile untokenizes them, and _UpdateAstString swaps a single string token while preserving its quote character [depot_tools/gclient_eval.py:895-909]. SetRevision follows Var() indirection — a dep spelled Var('v8_revision') is rolled by rewriting the variable, not the URL — pins an unpinned dep by appending @<rev>, and refuses multi-line or implicitly concatenated strings [depot_tools/gclient_eval.py:1137-1151]. SetCIPD strips a 'version:' + Var(…) prefix before writing; SetGCS may only change object_name, sha256sum, size_bytes and generation, and demands the same object count [depot_tools/gclient_eval.py:1076-1106; :1016-1043].
The surface, one paragraph each. `gclient getdep` (--var, -r path or path:package; exit 2 on a missing key) reads pins — from gitlinks when git_dependencies is SUBMODULES. `gclient setdep` writes them, and in SYNC or SUBMODULES state additionally stages the gitlink with `git update-index --add --cacheinfo 160000,<rev>,<path>` and prints "Changes have been staged" [depot_tools/gclient.py:5266-5335]. `roll-dep` is the human wrapper: it refuses a dirty tree, git-fetches the dep, resolves --roll-to (default origin/HEAD), calls gclient setdep, checks the dep out, rewrites the single `Revision:` line of README.chromium, and commits a message headed `Roll <dep>/ <from[:9]>..<to[:9]> (N commits)` [depot_tools/roll_dep.py:239-276; :143-184]. `gclient revinfo` (-s writes a snapshot .gclient pinning every dep into custom_deps), `gclient flatten` (one hermetic DEPS, --pin-all-deps expanding refs to full SHAs; note honestly that no consumer of flatten was identified, dossier PD-O4), `gclient recurse`, `gclient runhooks`, and `gclient gitmodules` (regenerates .gitmodules and stages gitlinks in chunks of 100) [depot_tools/gclient.py:4931-4989; :4058-4110; :3933-4055].
Then the gauntlet, because the reader should understand that a machine edit is only safe because five checks run after it. depot_tools' CheckForCommitObjects enforces DEPS/gitlink parity in SYNC state, with hard-coded exemptions only for ANGLE's third_party/dummy_chromium and Dawn's placeholder_chromium [depot_tools/presubmit_canned_checks.py:2875-3138; :3056-3066]. src/PRESUBMIT.py adds CheckNewDEPSHooksHasRequiredReviewers, CheckValidHostsInDEPSOnUpload (which shells out to `gclient verify`), CheckForNewDEPSDownloadFromGoogleStorageHooks (a ban on new download_from_google_storage hooks), CheckLibcxxRevisionsMatch (DEPS libcxx_revision must equal buildtools/deps_revisions.gni) and CheckUnwantedDependencies over added includes [src/PRESUBMIT.py:4050-4071; :8302-8330; :3555-3667]. One good aside: PRESUBMIT still runs CheckNoDEPSGIT for a file deleted from trunk in 2014 [src/PRESUBMIT.py:3341-3353] — evidence for the post's thesis about interfaces outliving their mechanism.
CODE EXCERPTS (2): depot_tools/gclient_eval.py:1137-1151 (SetRevision's Var-indirection branch and the '@' handling) and depot_tools/gclient.py:5314-5335 (the update-index --cacheinfo 160000 call, the RenderDEPSFile write, and the "Changes have been staged" message).
OWNED ELSEWHERE: who calls setdep at scale, and how often (§08); the SYNC state and why gitlinks exist (§09); clang's own use of setdep (§06).

sections.title: The roller fleet
sections.brief:
THESIS: Almost nobody rolls by hand. A fifth of chromium/src's commit stream is machine-written, continuously, and the machine deliberately does not use gclient.
AutoRoll describes itself as "a program which creates and manages DEPS rolls of a child project, eg. Skia, into a parent project, eg. Chrome" [skia.googlesource.com/buildbot/+/main/autoroll/README.md:3-20]. autoroll.skia.org listed 343 rollers on 2026-09-20, of which 158 target chromium/src main — the 152 whose parent is labelled "Chromium", the five AFDO rollers labelled "Chromium Main", and one labelled "Chromium main branch"; the remaining 30 target beta, stable, LTS, m109 and m114. Use these numbers exactly; the earlier "188 with a Chromium parent" reading was wrong (dossier D8/V06). Modes are RUNNING, DRY_RUN, STOPPED, OFFLINE; strategies BATCH, N_BATCH (N=20), SINGLE; defaults: ten-minute cooldown, three CQ attempts per CL, three CLs per target revision [autoroll/README.md:59-105]. The Go implementation avoids gclient on purpose: its own deps_parser rewrites the DEPS line and, when git_dependencies is SYNC or SUBMODULES, the gitlink too, uploading both through the Gerrit REST API [version_file_common.go:259-283]. Configs are text protos in the Googler-only skia-autoroll-internal-config repo (dossier PD-O1).
The traffic, measured. In the week 2026-09-14 to 2026-09-21 Gerrit merged 5,519 chromium/src changes across 22 branches, 4,513 on main; 940 (20.8%) were owned by the two Skia autoroll service accounts and 972 (21.5%) had subjects starting "Roll ". The gitiles log agrees commit-for-commit — the window is exactly Cr-Commit-Position #1697016..#1701528, and both the first and last commit of the week are rolls. Over four weeks the share is stable at 22.9% (3,893 of 16,973), peaking at 26.3% in the Labor-Day week because humans pause and rollers do not, and running 40–68% at weekends. Not every roll touches DEPS: 220 of the week's 940 roller commits are PGO-profile rolls changing one line of chrome/build/<platform>.pgo.txt, and 625 main commits (13.8%) touched DEPS at all, 591 of them roller-owned. Review reality: 3,428 of 3,893 four-week roll commits (88%) carry Tbr: and just 14 carry Reviewed-by. The tree's own HEAD, f288fed6, is itself an internal roll of clank/internal/apps.
Both directions, and the package systems. Reverse rolls exist: chromium-angle-autoroll lands "Roll Chromium from 40a71e004321 to ef3359c076e1 (970 revisions)" via ANGLE's roll_chromium_deps_v2.py, and V8's v8_auto_roller lands "Update V8 DEPS (trusted)". CIPD versions are an instance ID (base64url of sha256 plus a hash-algo byte, 44 chars), a unique tag such as git_revision:<hash> or version:3@1.12.1.chromium.4, or a ref like `latest`; the 153 packages break down as 76 instance IDs + 63 version: + 8 git_revision: + 4 version_file + 1 re_client_version: + 1 bare version_37.0.0 (dossier D7/V05). The 3pp pipeline uploads <prefix>/<pkg>/${platform} tagged version:<epoch>@<semver> — epoch 2 in the Python support_3pp module, 3@ in the Go pkgbuild loader — which is why the NDK is spelled 'version:' + Str('2@30.0.16248370'). Closing beat: the gn CIPD instance registered at 02:43Z on 2026-09-18 was rolled into DEPS by CL 8428489 created eight minutes later.

OWNED ELSEWHERE: setdep internals and presubmits (§07); the gitlink's meaning (§09); toolchain rolls (§06).

sections.title: Submodules, stage one, forever
sections.brief:
THESIS: Chromium announced a three-stage migration to native git submodules in 2023, executed stage one on schedule, and has been sitting there ever since — not because the mechanism failed but because the ecosystem around DEPS did not move.
The announcement, quoted. On 2 March 2023 Josip Sokcevic posted to chromium-dev that Chromium was "moving away from git dependencies being managed by gclient DEPS to native Git submodules", to "simplify tooling" and "unlock our long term vision of … getting the Chromium codebase with just git client". The design doc adds the concrete win — no more synthetic commit for codesearch/chromium/src — and defines three stages: submodules alongside DEPS (crbug 1409737, 2023 Q2), submodules as the source of truth with git deps removed from DEPS (crbug 1409734, 2023 Q4), and, aspirationally, git itself managing them (crbug 1417344, ETA unknown). Two boundary conditions matter: CIPD stays in DEPS ("we have no plans for CIPD dependencies"), and gclient stays in charge for stages 1–2. The mechanism doc introduced the git_dependencies key with its three states and the custom gclient-condition key native git ignores, and was candid that SUBMODULES breaks branch/HEAD pins, variable-based overrides and selective recursion [depot_tools/gclient_eval.py:20-24].
What landed: commit ef72622958e9, 23 August 2023, adding .gitmodules, 231 gitlinks and git_dependencies = 'SYNC'; M118 is the first release branch to carry it. Within hours developers reported submodules showing as uncommitted changes and `git cl upload` failures, and depot_tools spent months adding gclient gitmodules, installhooks, diff.ignoreSubmodules=dirty and fetch/push.recurseSubmodules=off.
Where it stands. Three years later the tree is in the same state and exactly consistent: 273 git deps, 273 .gitmodules sections, 273 gitlinks, zero mismatches, plus the vestigial SUBMODULE_MIGRATION var nothing reads [src/DEPS:580-582]. The obstacles are documented: the FAQ's own "Lots of Chromium infrastructure already parse DEPS file directly" [src/docs/git_submodules.md:249-253]; 49 *_revision vars .gitmodules cannot express [src/DEPS:340-444]; recursedeps with no git equivalent (gclient-recursedeps is written but never read) [depot_tools/gclient.py:1248-1249]; use_relative_paths still False; ANGLE's and Dawn's deliberately gitlink-less placeholders; and Cog. Name the real DEPS parsers: WebRTC's and ANGLE's rollers exec() Chromium's DEPS from gitiles, V8's roll_bisect.py regex-edits 'v8_revision', and CheckLibcxxRevisionsMatch. Only three Chromium-orbit repos reached SUBMODULES, all infrastructure: infra_superproject 2023-09-08, infra/infra 2025-03-07 ("having infra in the SYNC state is pretty annoying for dev-ex") and luci-py 2025-04-30.
Close with the advertised end state, measured. `git clone --recurse-submodules` parses Chromium's .gitmodules fine, but 85 of 273 submodules are on chrome-internal and fail anonymously, 144 conditions are ignored, git recurses into 25 nested .gitmodules gclient never touches, and nothing outside git happens — no CIPD, no GCS, no hooks, no gclient_args.gni. Put that list in a .callout, not a figure. Be explicit about what is not knowable: no public statement explains the slip from 2023 Q4, and bug 40254050 is open, last modified 2025-03-24, comments behind sign-in.

sections.title: What goma was, and why it ended
sections.brief:
THESIS: Goma solved the right problem with a bespoke protocol, and the protocol is what killed it. The engineering that survived is the include scanner.
What it was, quoted: "Goma hooks a compile request, and sends it to a backend compile server", so a build can run at -j500, with the backend caching results [infra/goma/client@5de52a5ece34 README.md]. Nico Weber described it publicly in June 2012 as "similar to pump-mode distcc, but google-internal". The client had two halves. gomacc — prepended to the compiler command, or symlinked in "masquerade mode" — parsed the flags, serialised an ExecReq and passed it to compiler_proxy over a unix socket. compiler_proxy was a multithreaded daemon whose CompileTask ran INIT → SETUP → FILE_REQ → CALL_EXEC → FILE_RESP → FINISHED, with LOCAL_OUTPUT / LOCAL_RUN / LOCAL_FINISHED for the local track. SETUP ran Goma's own directive-level C preprocessor: a macro environment (about 4,000 entries on Linux, over 15,000 on Windows because of windows.h), #if/#ifdef evaluated with a condition stack, #pragma once, include guards and #include_next honoured, and only the files a compiler would actually open inserted. Parsed directive lists lived in an IncludeCache sized for 140,000 entries; a DepsCache keyed by a SHA-256 command identifier skipped the walk entirely when FileStat and then the directive hash still validated. FILE_REQ uploaded content-addressed FileBlobs, embedding files under 2 MB and chunking larger ones; CALL_EXEC sent plain HTTP/1.1 protobuf to goma.chromium.org/cxx-compiler-service. Hermetic mode defaulted to "error": the backend had to use a compiler with the same version string and binary hash, or the task failed.
The transport is the pivot, and EngFlow named it: "Goma uses plain HTTP/1, so it needs lots of connections, and files need to be broken into chunks" — contrasted with RE-API's gRPC. By November 2020 Goma's backend was RBE-backed, making the Goma protocol a middleman; the same team then wrote reclient, mirroring gomacc→rewrapper and compiler_proxy→reproxy while keeping Goma's include scanner as the -gomaip flavour.
The end, as a dated ratchet. On 8 September 2023 (the archive timestamp is UTC, so US Pacific readers date it 7 September) Takuto Ikuta posted "PSA:Goma deprecation" to infra-dev, chromium-dev and chrome-build-team: "Goma will be deprecated by the end of January of next year", Google would "delete support for goma in Chromium builds around the beginning of 2024" and "stop maintaining the goma client and server". Then: gn gen warning 2023-09-26; last client roll 2023-09-27; a 5-second delay 2024-01-23; autoninja exiting for use_goma on Linux/macOS 2024-02-13 (Windows 02-21); CIPD package gone 2024-04-15; args deleted 2024-05-15; 2024-05-21 both repos reduced to "Goma is not maintained any more, please use reclient instead." Only fossils remain: goma-foundry-experiments, copy_staging_to_prod_and_goma.sh, the -gomaip suffix.
TWO CAUTIONS. The "30 minutes → 150 minutes" figure is from Bratell's June 2017 jumbo thread and measures Opera for Mac, not Chrome (dossier C06/V14). And say what was never published: fleet size, user counts, cache-hit rates, shutdown date.

OWNED ELSEWHERE: reclient, Siso and input discovery (§11).

Right third: the CompileTask state machine INIT → SETUP → FILE_REQ → CALL_EXEC → FILE_RESP → FINISHED with the parallel LOCAL_RUN / LOCAL_FINISHED track and the race outcomes. sections.title: reclient, RBE and Siso
sections.brief:
THESIS: Three GN args decide everything, Siso is the default everywhere, reclient survives as plumbing — and the deepest difference between the generations is not the transport but how each one decides what to upload.
Three args [src/build/toolchain/rbe.gni:25-31; siso.gni:5-22]: use_remoteexec defaults to false; use_siso defaults to true when gclient has written build/config/siso/.sisoenv, build_with_chromium is set and the out dir has no Ninja .ninja_deps; use_reclient = use_remoteexec && !use_siso. GN asserts remote execution needs one of the two clients, rejects cc_wrapper and a custom clang_base_path, requires the out dir be exactly two levels deep or "remote cache hits are basically zero", and since November 2025 warns "crbug.com/424659245 - Reclient is deprecated" [rbe.gni:56-69; src/BUILD.gn:1649-1656]. GN serialises its decisions into out/<dir>/gn_logs.txt, and that file — not args.gn — is what Siso's starlark reads. Print the literal args: developers set `use_remoteexec = true` and `use_siso = true` in args.gn plus `rbe_instance: projects/rbe-chromium-untrusted/instances/default_instance` in .gclient; 867 generated gn-args files carry `use_remoteexec=true use_siso=true use_reclient=false`.
Reclient today: binaries download only when download_reclient (default checkout_chromeos) is true, pinned at re_client_version:0.185.0.db415f21-gomaip; depot_tools' manifest keeps 0.124.1 "only for ChromeOS build" [src/DEPS:297-307; cipd_manifest.txt:81-83] — two files, dossier D3. Where it runs, rewrapper -cfg=<cfg> -exec_root=<root> wraps every compile and reclient_helper.py brackets the build with bootstrap --re_proxy and racing defaults (RBE_local_resource_fraction=0.2, RBE_racing_bias=0.95). Siso-native Windows and macOS builds still parse rewrapper cfgs for platform properties [rbe.gni:91-94].
Siso: a Ninja-compatible Go build tool with a built-in REAPI client, a digest-based filesystem and starlark configs, pinned as CIPD build/siso/${platform} at git_revision:22353054 [src/DEPS:291-292]. The configure_siso hook writes .sisoenv and copies a backend config (google.star for the eleven known Google RBE projects) defining platforms `default` and `large`; main.star builds the step config from gn args and gn_logs.txt, force-disabling remote unless gn_logs says use_remoteexec=true. Real rules: clang compiles remote, 2 m timeout; links on `large`, 10 m (80 m under ThinLTO), never on darwin; mojom generators on `large` only under googlechrome (880 ms on n2-highmem-8 vs 2.43 s on n2-custom-2-3840); ~70 Python/node scripts local-only. Limits derive from the machine: step 512×CPUs, scandeps 2×, local = CPUs, remote 80×CPUs. On bots, 866 of 1,066 builders carry $build/siso; five *-build-perf-developer builders keep $build/reclient.
h3 — WHAT EACH GENERATION UPLOADS. The input-root digest is half the action digest. Goma computed the exact set with a real preprocessor; reclient kept that engine (-gomaip links the goma-input-processor fork). Siso inverts it: scandeps calls itself a "forged" scanner built "to construct inputs for remote execution", not to decide re-execution; it reads only #include "x", <x> and MACRO, ignores #if, and expands every recorded macro value — deliberate over-approximation. The superset is cheap because dir:headers directories are never scanned but attached as a Merkle TreeEntry digested once per build, only the root digest probed against the CAS (378.3 s → 373 s). Correct a repeated claim: fast-deps was deleted 2026-04-10 ("not possible to know whether the cached dependency information is still safely usable"); two-phase caching stays behind SISO_EXPERIMENTS, unset in Chromium.
CODE EXCERPTS (2): src/build/toolchain/siso.gni:5-22 and siso/scandeps/doc.go:14-34.
OWNED ELSEWHERE: goma (§10); toolchain pins (§06); gclient_args.gni (§03).

Goma: gomacc | compiler_proxy (INIT→SETUP→FILE_REQ→CALL_EXEC→FILE_RESP→FINISHED) | exact directive preprocessor (4k macros Linux / 15k Windows, DepsCache keyed by command SHA-256) | HTTP/1.1 + protobuf to /cxx-compiler-service | MEM/STORAGE/LOCAL_OUTPUT cache, hermetic mode "error". Reclient: rewrapper | reproxy | scandeps_server (-gomaip = the same Goma engine) | gRPC REAPI | RBE action cache. Siso: none (built in) | siso ninja | scandeps over-approximation + precomputed :headers subtrees + hashfs | native REAPI | RBE action cache, two-phase caching behind an experiment. sections.title: What this design buys, and what it costs
sections.brief: THESIS: Both halves of this system are sitting in a stable intermediate state, for the same reason, and that reason is the design's price. Write this as an argument, not a summary — no new mechanism, only claims the earlier sections have already paid for. What it buys, with the evidence already on the page. (1) One text file is the whole dependency graph, so a roll is a one-line edit and a machine can make it 940 times a week — the fifth of the commit stream measured in §08 exists because editing DEPS is cheap and safe. (2) Hermeticity by declaration: the compiler, the sysroot, the SDK, the Python interpreter and the build tool are all pinned in the same file, so `gclient sync` plus `gn gen` reproduces a toolchain without installing anything — and GN will refuse to build if the two disagree ("Did you forget to gclient sync?"). (3) Conditions mean one description serves every platform: 320 of 451 entries are conditional, and a default Linux x64 host materialises 195 of them. (4) The declarative layer is transport-agnostic — the same file names git repos, CIPD packages and GCS objects, and the clang migration from hook to first-class GCS dep in June 2024 changed no consumer. What it costs. (1) A parse-only grammar is still a grammar: _SafeFormatter, the schema, the condition whitelist and the token-preserving editor exist because DEPS must be machine-editable and untrusted at once. (2) Interfaces outlive mechanisms. Name the survivors the post has already shown: git_dependencies = 'SYNC' three years after a stage 2 scheduled for 2023 Q4; rewrapper cfgs parsed by Siso on Windows and macOS purely for platform properties; reclient pinned a year after its announced removal; PRESUBMIT still checking for a .DEPS.git deleted from trunk in 2014; SUBMODULE_MIGRATION, a var nothing reads. (3) Every parser of DEPS is a dependency on DEPS. That is the FAQ's own stated reason for the two-stage migration — "Lots of Chromium infrastructure already parse DEPS file directly" — and the reason stage 2 has not happened. (4) The bytes: ≈25.1 GB of unique content before a single object file, of which 94% is git history that the build does not read. (5) Expressiveness that git cannot represent — 49 *_revision vars, recursedeps, conditions — is exactly what blocks the "just git clone" end state. Close on the pattern, stated once: the declarative file is easy to change and the ecosystem around it is not, so Chromium keeps the old interface alive while the new mechanism carries the load underneath. That sentence is the whole post. Then one honest forward-looking paragraph with its uncertainty marked reconstruction: nothing in the tree says stage 2 is abandoned, and nothing says it is scheduled; the same is true of reclient's removal. Do not predict dates. NO NEW CITATIONS should be needed here; every claim should point back to a section. Keep it short and declarative. Do not restate the sources list — that is §13.

figures.shows: Two-column ledger, one row per property of the design: column A "what it buys", column B "what the same property costs", with a third narrow column naming the section and the evidence. Rows: one declarative file (cheap rolls ↔ every parser becomes a dependency); pinned-in-text toolchain (reproducible without installs ↔ rolls need bots, promotion and a GN assert); conditions (one file for all platforms ↔ git submodules cannot express them); three transports (right tool per artefact ↔ three failure modes and three caches); gclient owns the tree (uniform on dev and bot ↔ `git clone` is not a checkout); SYNC dual-writing (safe migration ↔ a state now three years old).

sections.title: Sources
sections.brief:
THESIS: This section is the receipt. Make it usable: grouped, annotated with what each source was used FOR, and followed by a provenance footnote that is specific about what was not verified.
